headline: Computational tools link molecular dynamics, single-particle motion, and self-assembly
label: Biomolecular Conformational Ensemble Modelling
summary: Coarse-grained and multiscale simulations now resolve crowded mRNA, cellular nucleoids, and structure-derived assembly at the ensemble level.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational frameworks that extend from atomic or single-molecule data to ensemble- and mesoscale behaviour. ExaTrack benchmarks single-particle tracking analysis that models diffusive, directed, and confined motion with transition kinetics. PySteMoDA automates analysis of constant-velocity steered molecular dynamics, including force peaks. A Kremer-Grest bead-spring study reports that ribosome crowding shifts polysomal mRNA scaling toward quasi-2D conformations. ioNERDSS converts 3D atomic structures into coarse-grained models for rule-based self-assembly, and a coarse-grained JCVI-Syn3A model attributes nucleoid expansion to positively charged proteins screening ribosome-DNA repulsion. What is new is coupling structure-derived coarse graining and trajectory analysis to population-level observables in crowded or cellular contexts.
